title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over in Kansas after a Flock camera flagged their minivan as possibly stolen. Their KU Alumni plate had the number 7007, and a stolen GMC pickup had a temporary Kansas tag with the same number but a different background. Colwich police knew their vehicle and corrected the entry. About a month later, in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock camera led police to stop them at gunpoint and handcuff Matthew before realizing the mistake.

Kansas duplicates plate numbers across more than 100 designs, about half specialty plates, and Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate backgrounds. Wichita police Capt. Casey Slaughter said Flock alerts alone are not enough, but a wrong plate type entered into the system can force a stop. The state is moving to seven digit, non duplicated numbers. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops, and they hope to keep their 14 year old plate.
